transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because… I just can’t seem to settle down inside. Even when I’m tired and should be sitting still, I feel like I have to get up and do the next thing. It’s been hard.
Did this restless feeling start around the time you began taking a new medication or changed the dose of one you were already on?
I don’t think so… I mean, I can’t really tie it to any medication change. Nothing stands out to me that way.
Has this restless, need-to-move feeling been present nearly every day for months, or did it come on more suddenly over a shorter period?
It’s been… not sudden, no. It’s been a real problem since my husband died, almost two years ago now. About a year and ten months.
Do you find that you still have intense longing or preoccupying thoughts about your husband that come up throughout most days, even now, almost two years later?
I… I don’t know. I think about him, of course, but I’m not sure I’d say it’s like that most of the day. It’s hard to put into words.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or empty, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, for most of the day nearly every day?
I’m… not really sure how to answer that. I’ve had low days, yes, but whether it’s most of the day nearly every day… I don’t know. I don’t really keep track like that.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—more than the situation seems to call for—and having a hard time controlling that worry?
I don’t know… I mean, I worry some, like anyone would. But I’m not sure it’s a lot of different things, or that I can’t control it. I haven’t really thought about it that way.
Since your husband passed, do you find yourself having unwanted, intrusive memories or images of his death, or going out of your way to avoid people, places, or things that remind you of it?

I’m not sure. I mean… certain things do remind me of it, but I don’t know if I’d call them intrusive memories. I don’t think I go out of my way exactly… I just don’t really think about it in those terms.
Since your husband died, have you noticed feeling unusually on edge, easily startled, or constantly watchful, even when nothing seems to be wrong?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed that. I mean, I can get tense sometimes, but I’m not sure it’s like being constantly watchful or anything.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities or things you used to enjoy, even when you try to do them?
I’m not really sure. I still do some things, but I guess I haven’t paid much attention to whether I enjoy them the same way. It’s hard to say.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep—like trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual—nearly every night recently?
I don’t really know. My sleep’s never something I kept close track of. Some nights are different, I guess, but I couldn’t say it’s nearly every night or anything.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight—eating noticeably more or less than usual—over the past couple of weeks?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been watching my weight or anything. Eating’s just… kind of whatever lately, but I couldn’t say it’s noticeably more or less.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy nearly every day recently, even when you haven't been especially active?
I don’t really know. I get tired sometimes, but I haven’t been paying attention to whether it’s nearly every day or anything like that.
Since your husband died, has your grief and these feelings been affecting your ability to function—like managing daily tasks, work, or relationships—most days?

Yes… it has. I don’t like saying that, but my family’s had to help with bills and paperwork. And some things at church and with the garden… people had to cover for me or change plans because I didn’t follow through. It’s embarrassing. I feel like they don’t really count on me the same way now.
Since your husband died, do you often feel like part of your own identity or sense of self died with him, or that life feels meaningless or hard to make sense of without him?
I… I’m not sure how to answer that. I miss him, of course, but saying part of me died sounds… I don’t know. I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Since your husband died, do you still find it hard to accept or believe that he's really gone, even now?
I don’t know… some days it still feels unreal, I guess. But I haven’t really thought about it in those words.
I’m not sure. I mean… I know he’s gone. It’s just hard to talk about it like that.
Would you say that on most days, you experience a strong, persistent longing or yearning to be with your husband again?
I don’t know… I miss him, yes. But “most days” and “strong longing”... I’m not sure I’d put it that way. It’s hard to say.
Would you say your low mood and trouble getting things done happen mainly when something reminds you of your husband, or do you feel that way pretty much all the time, no matter what you're doing?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid attention to it that closely. Sometimes things remind me of him, sure, but… I don’t know if that’s the main reason. It kind of all runs together.
Would you say that thoughts of missing your husband and wanting him back are with you nearly every day, or do they come and go depending on the day?
I’m not sure. Some days it’s there more than others, I guess. I don’t really keep track of it that way.
Would you say that these feelings of longing for your husband and the trouble managing daily tasks have been happening consistently for at least the past year, or did they start more recently?
It’s been… since he died, really. That was about a year and ten months ago. That’s when things started being hard like this.
